name: Nzanyi
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Only atlas/classification refs (Blench 2019 Atlas, ALCAM 2012); no phonology or grammar located online

tone_statements.citation: Harley, Matthew. 2021. Nominal and verbal plurality in the Mandara and Ɓata subgroups of Central Chadic. Afrika und Übersee 94: 91-126. Hamburg: Hamburg University Press. DOI 10.15460/auue.2021.94.1.223 (CC BY 4.0; open PDFhttps://journals.sub.uni-hamburg.de/hup1/afrikaunduebersee/article/download/223/169)
tone_statements.quote: Tones were not always marked in the sources consulted, or were marked only sporadically without explanation. In this paper they have been marked when available and relevant to the discussion. In some languages, many of the mor- phemes concerned, including many verb roots, are inherently tone- less and receive their tone from the wider context.
tone_statements.locator: p. 95, end of section 2 'The Central Chadic languages' (data sources); Nzanyi tone-marked forms in section 4.3, Table 29 'Nzanyi plural nouns (data from Benson 2013)' and Table 30, pp. 116-117
tone_statements.summary: No analysis; Nzanyi nouns transcribed with a two-way H (acute) / L (grave) marking on each syllable, verbs unmarked; group-level remark that many verb roots are toneless and take tone from context.

sources.locator: p. 95, end of section 2 'The Central Chadic languages' (data sources); Nzanyi tone-marked forms in section 4.3, Table 29 'Nzanyi plural nouns (data from Benson 2013)' and Table 30, pp. 116-117
sources.note: Not a tone study and gives no statement of the Nzanyi tone inventory. It is, however, the only open, linguist-authored primary Nzanyi data located: the singular/plural nouns in Tables 29-30 (from Benson 2013 ms.) are transcribed with two tone marks, acute (H) and grave (L), e.g. [sə́] 'thing', [wó] 'corpse', [múɾə́] 'man', [vìnə́] 'room' ~ pl. [vènə̀gí], [gàsə́] 'leaf', [ɾɨ̀gʷá] 'road' ~ [ɾàgʷàgí]; the plural verbs in Table 31 are left unmarked. The methods note (p. 95) says tones were marked only where the sources had them and that in some of these languages many morphemes, incl. verb roots,…

sources.citation: Benson, Ishya. 2014. Nzanyi grammar write-up 2014. Jos: Theological College of Northern Nigeria. xii+69 pp. (unpublished manuscript)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, not open: the recorded link leads to a login, a search-only view or a restricted repository; the linked copy is not accessible
sources.note: The only description of Nzanyi in existence (Glottolog's sole descriptive reference; Blench Atlas 'Grammar: Benson (2014)'); a 69-page grammar write-up from a TCNN/NBTT translation programme almost certainly opens with a phonology section that would state the tone system and any stress remark. Glottolog (Harald Hammarström) holds a PDF copy.
